Neglecting absorption by the polarizers and given that the first polarizer's axis is parallel to the plane of polarization of the incident light, the intensity of light at the exit of the fifth polarizer is closest to -
options: same as that of the incident light
questions.solution: $\mathrm{I}=\mathrm{I}_{0}\left(\cos ^{2} \phi\right)^{4}=\mathrm{I}_{0} \times\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^{4}=30 \%$ of $\mathrm{I}_{0}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A speaker emits a sound wave of frequency $f_{0}$. When it moves towards a stationary observer with speed $u$, the observer measures a frequency $f_{1}$. If the speaker is stationary, and the observer moves towards it with speed $\mathrm{u}$, the measured frequency is $f_{2}$. Then -
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{f}_{1}=\frac{\mathrm{f}_{0}[\mathrm{v}]}{\mathrm{v}-\mathrm{u}}$
$f_{2}=f_{0} \frac{[v+u]}{v}f_{2}-f_{1}=f_{0}\left(\frac{u+v}{v}-\frac{v}{v-u}\right)f_{2}-f_{1}=\frac{-u^{2} f_{0}}{(v)(v-u)}=-v e\therefore f_{1} \gt f_{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: At $23^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, a pipe open at both ends resonates at a frequency of 450 hertz. At what frequency does the same pipe resonate on a hot day when the speed of sound is 4 percent higher than it would be at $23^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ ?
questions.solution: $\mathrm{f} \lambda=\mathrm{v}\mathrm{f} \propto \mathrm{v}\frac{\mathrm{f}_{1}}{\mathrm{f}_{2}}=\frac{\mathrm{v}_{1}}{\mathrm{v}_{2}}\frac{450}{\mathrm{f}_{2}}=\frac{\mathrm{v}_{1}}{1.04 \mathrm{v}_{1}}\mathrm{f}_{2}=1.04 \times 450=468 \mathrm{~Hz}$
